rules.statement: Don't ask an extension member to drop its null guard on the receiver because the method it delegates to repeats the same check: extension members must guard the receiver themselves, since they can be called on null.
rules.why: The conventions require every extension member to guard its receiver against null. Its tests pin what a caller sees, an ArgumentNullException for a null receiver, whichever check throws it.
rules.check: Before reporting a duplicated null check, see whether the method is an extension member (a `this` parameter or an extension block) and the check is on the receiver; if so, don't report it.

rules.statement: A plain (non-extension) overload that only delegates to another overload doing the same argument null check, with the same parameter name, should not repeat that check.
rules.why: A rule that guards data has one implementation. Copies can drift apart, and tests named for the outer check don't pin it because the inner check throws the same exception.
rules.check: Look for `ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull` (or a similar guard) in a convenience overload whose body forwards the same argument to an overload that guards it the same way. Make sure the `<exception>` docs still hold after the check is removed.
